summary:
Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive learning experience that takes users through the journey of a Mars mission, helping them understand what it takes to explore another planet. Instead of learning about space through information alone, users experience different mission stages and make decisions along the way, from choosing a landing site and protecting astronauts from radiation to building a habitat, handling emergencies, and communicating with Earth.

The project addresses the challenge of making space science more engaging and accessible by turning complex scientific concepts into an interactive mission simulation. It combines educational content with real space research and mission-related information to help users explore the challenges of human spaceflight.

Our goal is to encourage curiosity, improve understanding of Mars exploration, and make learning about astronaut missions more engaging through an experience that combines exploration, decision-making, and science.
details:
Project Details – Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive educational website designed to introduce people to astronaut training and space exploration. It is not just a Mars simulation game; it is a complete learning experience that takes users from understanding the basics of space science to exploring the challenges of real space missions.

The website combines educational modules, interactive activities, quizzes, mini-games, progress tracking, and mission simulations in one platform. It is designed for beginners and anyone interested in learning about space, without requiring previous knowledge of astronautics.

1. Astronaut Learning Academy

The website provides educational content that introduces users to important topics related to astronaut training and space missions, including:

  • Space Science: Understanding the space environment, planets, space weather, and the conditions astronauts face beyond Earth.
  • Space Radiation: Learning about radiation in space, its sources, and its possible effects on astronauts.
  • Astronaut Health: Exploring how spaceflight affects the human body through real space research.
  • Spacecraft Systems: Learning about essential spacecraft systems such as oxygen, water, power, and food supplies.
  • Mission Preparation: Understanding the challenges astronauts must prepare for before and during a mission.

The lessons are supported by interactive explanations, quizzes, and activities to help users understand and remember the information.

2. Interactive Learning and Mini-Games

Instead of relying only on reading, users can interact with what they learn through quizzes, challenges, and mini-games. These activities help them test their knowledge, make decisions, and understand scientific concepts through practical examples.

The platform is designed to make learning more engaging while encouraging curiosity, critical thinking, and problem-solving.

3. Learning Progress and Assessment

The learning experience includes a structured progression system that helps users follow their journey through the different learning topics.

Users can track their progress, complete activities, test their understanding, and work toward completing different learning stages. The goal is to make astronaut learning feel like a continuous journey rather than a collection of unrelated lessons.

4. Mars Mission Simulation

One of the main interactive experiences on the website is the Mars Mission Simulation.

Users go through a mission journey, starting with spacecraft preparation and continuing through different stages of exploring Mars.

The simulation includes:

  • Selecting a suitable Mars landing site.
  • Understanding radiation risks and protection methods.
  • Building a Mars habitat and considering essential resources such as solar power and life-support systems.
  • Responding to possible mission emergencies.
  • Managing communication with Earth and understanding communication delays.

Users explore different situations, make decisions, and learn why each stage matters for the success and safety of a Mars mission.

5. NASA Data and Scientific Resources

An important part of the website is connecting educational content with real space science.

We used NASA resources such as Mars exploration information, radiation measurements, and astronaut research to support the learning material and mission scenarios.

Resources such as NASA's Open Science Data Repository (OSDR), Mars radiation research, DONKI, and NASA's Mars exploration resources help provide scientific context for different learning topics.

6. Tools and Development

The project uses structured JSON to organize educational content, mission stages, scenarios, and simulation information.

AI tools supported different parts of the development process:

  • ChatGPT: Assisted with development, content organization, simulation structures, and documentation.
  • Claude: Assisted with reviewing technical structures and improving development content.
  • Google NotebookLM: Helped research and organize information from scientific sources, including NASA materials.

The team reviewed and adapted AI-assisted outputs and used scientific sources to support the educational information.

7. Creativity and Intended Impact

What makes Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer different is that it combines learning and practical mission experiences in one website.

Users do not simply read about becoming an astronaut. They learn the science behind space exploration, test their knowledge, follow their progress, and eventually apply what they have learned through interactive mission scenarios.

Our goal is to make astronaut training concepts more accessible to a wider audience, encourage interest in science and engineering, and help people better understand the scientific, technical, and human challenges involved in exploring other planets.

During development, we considered scientific accuracy, accessibility for beginners, educational value, ease of navigation, and the importance of connecting every interactive experience to real space exploration challenges.
